name: PageSchema Studio
author: Anil

sections.description:
PageSchema Studio adds a schema builder to your editor so search engines understand your content and your pages can qualify for rich results — without editing theme files or writing JSON by hand.

Main features

  • 10 schema types — Article, WebPage, Product, Local Business, Video, How-To, Person, Organization, Website and BreadcrumbList
  • Auto-filled fields — title, excerpt, featured image, author and dates come from your post and stay up to date
  • Live preview — see an approximate Google result, the JSON-LD code and validation checks while you edit
  • Validation — checks against Google’s required and recommended properties, on every post and on the dashboard
  • FAQ block — show questions on the page and add them to the FAQPage schema in one step
  • Manual JSON-LD — paste your own code; it’s checked as you type, and its type and fields are filled in automatically
  • Sitewide schema — Organization and WebSite on every page, linked to your articles and pages
  • Defaults per content type — give every post (or custom post type) a schema without editing each one
  • Schema Sources — scan a page to see schema from other plugins, and turn off Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO or WooCommerce schema
  • Dashboard & Help Center — schema coverage and health across your site, plus answers to common questions
  • English and French — switch the plugin’s language from the top right of its screens

Developers can add their own schema types by extending Pageschema_Type, and adjust the output with filters.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the anilsuwal-pageschema-studio folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to PageSchema Studio → Settings to describe your site and choose a default schema for each content type.
  4. Edit any post or page and use the “PageSchema Studio — Schema” box (or the “Schema” panel in the block editor sidebar).
sections.faq:
Will this conflict with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

They also output schema, so a page could describe the same thing twice. Use PageSchema Studio → Schema Sources to scan a page and turn their schema off with one switch.

Do I have to set up every post by hand?

No. In Settings → Content types, choose a default schema for each content type (for example Article for posts). Fields fill in from the post automatically.

Can I paste my own JSON-LD?

Yes, in the “Manual JSON-LD” box. It is checked as you type, the matching schema type is selected, and its fields are filled from your code.

Is the Google preview exactly what Google will show?

No. It approximates a typical result. Valid schema makes a page eligible for rich results; Google decides whether to show them.

Why don’t my FAQs show in Google?

Google currently shows FAQ rich results only for well-known government and health sites. The markup is still valid and other search engines use it.

Does it work with custom post types?

Yes. Enable them in Settings → Content types.

More answers are in PageSchema Studio → Help Center.
sections.changelog:
1.2.1

  • Changed: plugin renamed to PageSchema Studio.

1.2.0

  • New: Product, Local Business, Video and How-To schema types.
  • New: live preview in the editor — Google result, JSON-LD and validation checks.
  • New: FAQ (Schema) block.
  • New: manual JSON-LD is validated as you type and fills in the matching type and fields.
  • New: default schema per content type, and custom post type support.
  • New: Schema Sources screen to scan pages and turn off schema from other plugins.
  • New: redesigned dashboard and settings, and a Help Center.
  • New: French translation with a per-user language switcher.
  • Improved: connected schema — articles name your Organization as publisher, pages link to your WebSite.
  • Changed: requires WordPress 6.3 or later.

1.1.1

  • Fixed: per-post schema fields were saved under lowercased keys and never output. Existing data is repaired automatically on update.
  • Fixed: manual JSON-LD property names (e.g. mainEntity, sameAs) were lowercased. Manual JSON-LD saved with 1.1.0 needs to be re-entered.
  • Security: JSON-LD output now escapes < and >, and manual JSON-LD keys are restricted to valid property names.
  • Fixed: clearing manual JSON-LD or FAQ items on upgraded sites no longer brings back pre-1.1.0 values. Legacy _pss_* meta is removed.
  • Changed: blank fields use the live post value (title, dates, image…) instead of a saved copy, so dateModified stays current.
  • Fixed: the Google Rich Results Test link now uses the post’s public URL, and appears once the post is published.
  • Added: missing-field and invalid-JSON warnings appear in the block editor.
  • Fixed: “Use existing SEO title & description” expands Yoast/RankMath template variables.
  • Dashboard: status reflects what is actually output, multi-type JSON-LD is labelled correctly, and Quick Add links open the editor.
  • Fixed: Settings page styles not loading on translated admin screens.

1.1.0

  • Renamed all plugin prefixes from pss to pageschema for WordPress.org compliance.
  • Removed FAQ output cap and freemium marketing copy.
  • Added proper validation and recursive sanitization for manual JSON-LD input.
  • Added database migration for existing installs using legacy pss_* keys.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
